chapters.1.lds: The 2026 lesson reads the rescue as another opportunity for Jonah to respond. How do the sailors’ actions contrast with Jonah’s flight?
chapters.1.summary: The LORD tells Jonah to go and preach against the great city of Nineveh. Jonah boards a ship going the other way. The LORD sends a violent storm. The sailors pray to their gods and throw the cargo overboard. Jonah is asleep below. The lot points to him, and he tells them to throw him in. The men row hard for land and then do as he says. The sea grows calm, and a great fish swallows Jonah.
chapters.2.lds: The lesson invites readers to notice God’s mercy throughout Jonah’s experience. How does Jonah’s promise compare with the sailors’ earlier worship?
chapters.2.summary: Jonah prays to the LORD from inside the fish. He says he called from the depths, and God heard him. The waters closed over him, and weeds wrapped his head. He sank to the roots of the mountains. God brought his life up from the pit. Jonah says idol worshipers give up their hope of mercy. He will offer thanks and pay his vows. The LORD speaks to the fish, and it puts Jonah on dry land.
chapters.3.lds: The lesson connects Nineveh’s change with sharing the gospel despite uncertain expectations. Why does God’s response focus on changed conduct?
chapters.3.summary: The LORD’s word comes to Jonah a second time, and he goes. He walks a day into the city. He says that in forty days Nineveh will be overthrown. The people believe God and put on sackcloth. The king leaves his throne and sits in ashes. He orders everyone to fast, pray, and turn from violence. He says God may yet relent. God sees that they have turned, and he does not destroy them.
chapters.4.lds: The lesson asks readers to consider mercy toward others when Jonah resents their rescue. Whose lives does God include in the final question?
chapters.4.summary: Jonah is very angry that Nineveh is spared. He says this is why he fled in the first place. He knew God is gracious, merciful, and slow to anger. He asks to die. He sits outside the city to see what will happen. God gives him a plant for shade and then sends a worm to kill it. Jonah is angry enough to die. God asks whether he should not care for a great city and its animals.
